Thanks — quick first pass below. I ran a couple of scenarios in the attached workbook (edgewise-econ-scenarios.xlsx). Key assumptions: 20M tokens/mo, baseline list pricing, and expected onboarding effort = ~120 engineer-hours (SSO, SCIM, KV export/import and validation).

Offer A — Aggressive match (fast close):
- 15% committed discount on a 12-month term (structured so the first 3 months are effectively deeper via onboarding credit)
- Onboarding credit = 3 months of committed spend credited back as invoice credit (applied month 4)
- 40 hours of dedicated migration support + 60 hours standard support during ramp
- Win condition: net-first-year price within ~3% of competitor offer; faster procurement cycle.

Offer B — Balanced (better margin):
- 10% committed discount on a 12-month term
- 1-month onboarding credit + option for a usage-based rebate if they exceed 25M tokens/month during Q3/Q4 (5% rebate on incremental usage)
- 80 hours migration support (mixed remote + 2 onsite days if requested)

Margin impact: Offer A compresses gross margin by ~7–9 points in year one depending on how the onboarding credit is structured; Offer B compresses by ~3–5 points but preserves upside if usage grows.

Recommendation: Lead with Offer A if the procurement timeline is the critical factor and they need a tight net-first-year price. Offer B if they are more focused on long-term TCO and less on immediate headline parity.

Attachments: edgewise-econ-scenarios.xlsx
